title: The Wisdom of Haykar the Sage
summary: Haykar was the venerable Grand Vizier to King Sennacherib of Assyria, renowned across the ancient world for his peerless wisdom and righteousness. Having no son of his own, Hayk...
keywords: the say of haykar the sage
full_text:
Haykar was the venerable Grand Vizier to King Sennacherib of Assyria, renowned across the ancient world for his peerless wisdom and righteousness. Having no son of his own, Haykar adopted his nephew, Nadan, raising him with lavish affection and teaching him the proverbs of statecraft, morality, and honor.

Yet Nadan grew proud, ungrateful, and covetous. Eager to seize his uncle's wealth and office, Nadan forged treasonous letters in Haykar's handwriting to the rival King of Egypt, making it appear that the wise vizier was plotting to betray Assyria!

Deceived by the forged scrolls, King Sennacherib was consumed by wrath and ordered his chief executioner, Abu Samik, to put Haykar to death.
However, Abu Samik had once been saved from an unjust accusation by Haykar years before. The executioner could not bring himself to harm his benefactor:
'Master Haykar,' whispered Abu Samik, 'I will slay a condemned criminal in thy place, and conceal thee in a secret underground vault beneath thy garden until truth is revealed.'

Haykar was hidden in the vault, while Nadan strutted into the palace, took his uncle's properties, and began squandering the estate on cruel pleasures.

Soon after, Pharaoh of Egypt, believing Haykar was dead and Assyria was defenseless, sent an impossible challenge to King Sennacherib:
'Send me a sage who can build a castle in the air between heaven and earth, and answer all riddles of the Sphinx. If thou failest, thou shalt pay Egypt three years of imperial tribute!'

Sennacherib searched his kingdom in panic, but none could match the challenge. Nadan trembled and fled into hiding.
The King wept aloud: 'Alas! Would that my wise father Haykar were alive! I would give half my kingdom to look upon his face!'

Abu Samik fell to his knees: 'Rejoice, O King! Haykar lives!'

Haykar was brought forth from the vault. Sennacherib embraced him with tears of repentance and begged him to save the empire.
Haykar traveled to Egypt. Using eagles trained to carry ropes into the clouds with light baskets holding young boys who shouted down building instructions, Haykar demonstrated the 'castle in the air'! He then answered every riddle of Pharaoh's priests with dazzling brilliance, compelling Pharaoh to pay three years' tribute to Assyria!

Returning triumphant to Nineveh, Haykar requested only one thing: custody of his treacherous nephew Nadan.
He brought Nadan before him, but instead of executing him, Haykar sat him down and recited the immortal Proverbs of Haykar:
'My son, he who digs a pit for his brother shall fall into it himself; he who throws a stone into the sky will have it fall upon his own head. I planted thee like a cedar tree, but thou didst bear only bitter thorns.'

Overwhelmed by the crushing weight of his own guilt and his uncle's majestic mercy, Nadan's heart broke in shame.
Haykar resumed his vizierate, governing with eternal honor and leaving behind proverbs that guided kings and sages for three millennia.
moral: Unshakeable loyalty, profound wisdom, and forgiveness outshine envy and preserve kingdoms.

options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.

Believing rumors and flattery without proof
